title: Rewrite the exponent
text: Start by rewriting the power as a square of a square: $$\cos**4(\theta)=(\cos**2(\theta))**2.$$ Then apply the power-reducing formula for cosine.

title: First power reduction
text: The power-reducing formula is $$\cos**2(\theta)=\frac{1+\cos(2\theta)}{2}.$$ Substituting this in gives $$\left(\frac{1+\cos(2\theta)}{2}\right)**2.$$ Expand this squared expression.

title: Expand the square
text: Expanding the binomial yields $$\frac{1+2\cos(2\theta)+\cos**2(2\theta)}{4}.$$ We still have a squared trigonometric term, so we must apply the power-reducing formula a second time to the $$\cos**2(2\theta)$$ term.

title: Second power reduction
text: Be careful with the angle multiplier. Applying the formula to $$2\theta$$ yields $$\cos**2(2\theta)=\frac{1+\cos(4\theta)}{2}.$$

title: Substitute and simplify
text: Substitute this back into our expanded fraction: $$\frac{1+2\cos(2\theta)+\frac{1+\cos(4\theta)}{2}}{4}.$$ To clear the nested fraction, multiply the top and bottom of the main fraction by $$2$$ to get $$\frac{2+4\cos(2\theta)+1+\cos(4\theta)}{8}.$$

title: Combine like terms
text: Combine the constants in the numerator to get your final equivalent expression: $$\frac{3$$ + 4\cos(2\theta) + \cos(4\theta)}{8}$$.
